label: eq:Lu
title: Proof
body_md:
Let  us write $\mathfrak{b}=\mathfrak{b}_1\mathfrak{b}_2$, where $\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1$ is square-free and 
$\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ is square-full, with $\gcd(\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1,\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2)=1$. 
Then 
$
g(\mathfrak{b})=
\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2 \operatorname{N}\mathfrak{h},
$
where 
$\mathfrak{h}$ is the greatest common ideal divisor of $\mathfrak{b}_1$ and $N$.
In summary, we may now write
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Lu}
L(u)\leqslant 
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2\ll X\\ \text{$\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ square-full}}}\sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2}
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1\ll X/(\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{b}_2)\\ 
\operatorname{N}{{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_1 \ll Y/\operatorname{N}{{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_2\\
\gcd(\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{b}_1,\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{b}_2)=1}} \mu^2(\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1) 
\sum_{\mathfrak{h}\mid (\mathfrak{b}_1,N)} \sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{h}}
\# \mathscr{C}(u,\mathfrak{b}_1\mathfrak{b}_2).
\end{equation}


In order to proceed, we assume without loss of generality that $u\in V$ satisfies
$$
\mathfrak{H}(L_1(u))\leqslant\cdots\leqslant \mathfrak{H}(L_m(u)).
$$
Let us write $\mathbf{c}=(\mathbf{c}',\mathbf{c}'')$, where $\mathbf{c}'=(c_1,\dots,c_m)$ and $\mathbf{c}''=(c_{m+1},\dots,c_n)$. 
Keeping in mind  \eqref{eq:squall}, we first fix  a choice of $\mathbf{c}''\in \left((\mathfrak{b}_1\mathfrak{b}_2)^{-1} {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_1 {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_2\right)^{n-m}$ satisfying
$$
|c_i^{(l)}| \ll 
P^{-1+\varepsilon}  Y^{1/d} |u_l| ,
$$
for $m+1\leqslant i\leqslant n$ and $1\leqslant l\leqslant d$.  We claim that 
 there exists
 $\lambda\in K$ such that 
$$(\lambda)=(\mathfrak{b}_1\mathfrak{b}_2)^{-1} {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_1 {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_2  \mathfrak{p}_2^{-1},
$$ 
for a suitable prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}_2$ of norm $O(P^\varepsilon)$. 
To begin with, it follows from part (ii) of Lemma \ref{lem:alg1} that
 there exists
 $\lambda_3\in \mathfrak{o}$ such that 
$(\lambda_3)=(\mathfrak{b}_1\mathfrak{b}_2)^{-1} {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_1 {{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_2  \mathfrak{p}_3$, for a suitable prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}_3$ of norm $O(P^\varepsilon)$. 
A second application of this result reveals that there exists $\lambda_2\in \mathfrak{o}$ and a prime ideal
$\mathfrak{p}_2$ of norm $O(P^\varepsilon)$, such that $(\lambda_2)=\mathfrak{p}_3\mathfrak{p}_2$. The claim now follows with 
$\lambda=\lambda_3/\lambda_2$.

On multiplying by units we can further assume that 
$$
X^{-1/d}Y^{1/d}\ll |\lambda^{(l)}|\ll X^{-1/d}Y^{1/d+\varepsilon},
$$
for $1\leqslant l\leqslant d$, on
recalling that  $\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2 \asymp X$ and
 $\operatorname{N}{{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_1\operatorname{N}{{}^{{G}}\mathfrak{b}}_2 \asymp Y$.
Making the change of variables $\mathbf{c}''=\lambda \mathbf{d}''$,
we deduce that 
for $m+1\leqslant i\leqslant n$, we have 
$d_i\in \mathfrak{o}$ and
$$
|d_i^{(l)}| \ll 
P^{-1+\varepsilon}  X^{1/d} |u_l| ,
$$
for  $1\leqslant l\leqslant d$.
In particular, 
if $\mathbf{c}''\neq \0$ then there exists $i\in \{m+1,\dots,n\}$ such that 
$$
1\leqslant |N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(d_i)| \ll 
P^{-d+\varepsilon}  X |\operatorname{Nm} (u)| .
$$
Recalling that 
 $\operatorname{Nm}(u)\leqslant \mathfrak{H}(u)\ll P^{d+\varepsilon}/X$, we deduce that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neq0-1}
\mathbf{c}''\neq \0 \Longrightarrow   
\frac{P^{d-\varepsilon}}{X}\ll 
\mathfrak{H}(u)\ll \frac{P^{d+\varepsilon}}{X}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, arguing as in Lemma \ref{lem:wish}, it readily  follows from a result in Lang
 \cite[Thm.~0 in \S V.1]{lang} that  
 the overall  number of  vectors $\mathbf{d}''$ is $O(P^\varepsilon)$.
We must next address the number of $\mathbf{c}'\in \mathfrak{o}^m$, with 
$(\mathbf{c}',\mathbf{c}'')\neq \0$, which satisfy
$$
|c_i^{(l)}| \ll 
P^{-1+\varepsilon} Y^{1/d} |\rho_l(L_i(u))|,
$$
for $1\leqslant i\leqslant m$ and $1\leqslant l\leqslant d$.
It is clear that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:neq0-2}
\mathbf{c}'\neq \0 \Longrightarrow   
1\ll P^{-d+\varepsilon} Y 
\mathfrak{H}(L_m(u)).
\end{equation}
Together,  \eqref{eq:neq0-1} and \eqref{eq:neq0-2} yield the first part of the lemma. 

Appealing once more to 
Lang
 \cite[Thm.~0 in \S V.1]{lang}, 
we deduce that 
  the number of $\mathbf{c}'$ is
  \begin{align*}
&\ll  \prod_{i=1}^{m}\left(1+  \prod_{l=1}^d
P^{-1+\varepsilon} Y^{1/d} |\rho_l(L_i(u))| 
\right)
\ll  J(u),
\end{align*}
in the notation of the lemma. 
Returning to 
\eqref{eq:Lu}, 
we deduce that 
\begin{align*}
L(u)
&\ll P^\varepsilon J(u)
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2\ll X\\ \text{$\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ square-full}}}\sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2}
\sum_{\mathfrak{h}\mid N} \sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{h}}
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_1\ll X/(\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{b}_2)\\ \mathfrak{h}\mid \mathfrak{b}_1}} 1\\
&\ll P^\varepsilon J(u)
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2\ll X\\ \text{$\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ square-full}}}\sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2}
\sum_{\mathfrak{h}\mid N} \sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{h}} \cdot \frac{X}{(\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{b}_2) (\operatorname{N} \mathfrak{h})}\\
&\ll P^\varepsilon X J(u)
\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2\ll X\\ \text{$\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ square-full}}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2}},
\end{align*}
since there are $O(1)$ ideal divisors $\mathfrak{h}\mid N$ when $N\in \mathfrak{o}$ is non-zero.
Finally, the lemma follows on noting that  there are $O(\sqrt{X})$ integral ideals such that $\operatorname{N}\mathfrak{b}_2$ is a square-full integer of modulus at most $X$.

title: Proof
body_md:
In the proof of this result we shall make  frequent use of the observation that 
\begin{align*}
\mathfrak{H}(L_i(u))
&=\prod_{l=1}^d \max\{1,|a_i^{(l)}u_l+b_i^{(l_\tau)}u_{l_\tau}|\}\ll \mathfrak{H}(u)^2,
\end{align*}
for any $i\in \{1,\dots,n\}$, which follows from \eqref{eq:carpet}.

We may assume without loss of generality  that  the range of integration is restricted to satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:moose}
\mathfrak{H}(L_1(u))\leqslant \cdots\leqslant \mathfrak{H}(L_m(u)).
\end{equation}
We further break the range of integration into $m+1$ regions.
For $0\leqslant t\leqslant m$, let  $R_t$ denote the set of 
$u\in V$ with 
$\mathfrak{H}(u)\leqslant P^{d+\varepsilon}/X$,
such that \eqref{eq:this} 
 and \eqref{eq:moose} hold, with 
$$
\mathfrak{H}(L_t(u))\ll P^{d-\varepsilon}/Y,\quad 
\mathfrak{H}(L_{t+1}(u))\gg P^{d-\varepsilon}/Y.
$$
(Note that the left inequality is vacuous when $t=0$, and similarly for the right hand inequality when $t=m$.) In particular, it is clear that 
$
R_m=\emptyset
$
when the second inequality in \eqref{eq:this} holds.
Moreover, 
when   $t\in \{1,\dots,m-1\}$, 
we observe that 
$$
R_t\neq  \emptyset \Longrightarrow
 Y\ll P^{d-\varepsilon},
$$
since $\mathfrak{H}(L_t(u))\geqslant 1$.
We have 
\begin{align*}
I(X,Y)
&\ll \sum_{t=0}^{m} P^\varepsilon
\int_{
 R_t}
\frac{\left(
(P^{-d} Y)^{m-t}  \mathfrak{H}(L_{t+1}(u))\cdots 
 \mathfrak{H}(L_{m}(u))\right)}{
{\sqrt{\mathfrak{H}(L_1(u))\cdots 
 \mathfrak{H}(L_m(u))
 \mathfrak{H}(u)^{n-m}}}}
 \mathrm{d} u.
 \end{align*}
 Thus
\begin{align*}
 I(X,Y)
&\ll
 \sum_{t=0}^{m}
 I^{(t)}(X,Y),
 \end{align*}
 where
$$
I^{(t)}(X,Y)=
(P^{-d} Y)^{m-t}P^\varepsilon
\int_{
 R_t}
\frac{\left(
  \mathfrak{H}(L_{t+1}(u))\cdots 
 \mathfrak{H}(L_{m}(u))\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{
{\mathfrak{H}(u)^{(n-m)/2}}}
 \mathrm{d} u,
$$
on taking 
$\mathfrak{H}(L_1(u))\cdots \mathfrak{H}(L_t(u))\geqslant 1$.
 

We first deal with 
$ I^{(0)}(X,Y)$.
Recalling that 
 $\mathfrak{H}(L_i(u))\ll \mathfrak{H}(u)^2$, for $1\leqslant i\leqslant m$, it follows that 
$$
\frac{\left(
  \mathfrak{H}(L_{1}(u))\cdots 
 \mathfrak{H}(L_{m}(u))\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{ \mathfrak{H}(u)^{(n-m)/2}}
\ll \mathfrak{H}(u)^{3m/2-n/2}.
$$
If $
3m/2-n/2\geqslant -1$, then 
 \eqref{eq:BoundB} yields
$$
\int_{
 R_0}
 \mathfrak{H}(u)^{3m/2-n/2} \mathrm{d} u \ll 
 P^\varepsilon \left(\frac{P^{d}}{X}\right)^{3m/2-n/2+1}.
 $$
 Alternatively, 
 if  $3m/2-n/2< -1$ then the left hand side is $O(1)$
 by 
  \eqref{eq:BoundC}.
Thus
\begin{align*}
 I^{(0)}(X,Y)
&\ll P^\varepsilon (P^{-d} Y)^{m}
\left( \left(\frac{P^{d}}{X}\right)^{3m/2-n/2+1}+1\right),
\end{align*}
which is satisfactory.

Terms with $1\leqslant t\leqslant m-1$ only contribute when $Y\leqslant P^d$. 
Arguing as above, 
it follows from
 \eqref{eq:BoundC} and \eqref{eq:BoundB}  that 
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{t=1}^{m-1}
 I^{(t)}(X,Y)
&\ll
 \sum_{t=1}^{m-1}
(P^{-d} Y)^{m-t}
\int_{
 R_t}
 \mathfrak{H}(u)^{3m/2-t-n/2}
 \mathrm{d} u\\
&\ll
P^\varepsilon \sum_{t=1}^{m-1}
(P^{-d} Y)^{m-t}
\left( \left(\frac{P^{d}}{X}\right)^{3m/2-t-n/2+1}+1\right)\\
&\ll
P^\varepsilon \sum_{t=1}^{m-1}
\left(
(P^{-d} Y)^{m}
 \left(\frac{P^{d}}{X}\right)^{3m/2-n/2+1}
\left(\frac{X}{Y}\right)^t
+
(P^{-d} Y)^{m-t}\right)\\
&\ll
P^\varepsilon \left\{ 
\frac{P^{d(m/2-n/2+1)}Y^{m-1}}{X^{3m/2-n/2}}+
 \frac{Y}{P^d}
\right\}.
\end{align*}
since $X\leqslant Y$. This is satisfactory for the lemma. 


It remains to 
estimate  $I^{(m)}(X,Y)$. In this case we may assume that  $u$  satisfies the  first inequality in 
\eqref{eq:this}, since $R_m=\emptyset$ otherwise. 
Hence
 \eqref{eq:BoundA} yields
\begin{align*}
I^{(m)}(X,Y)
&=
\int_{\{u \in V : 
P^{d-\varepsilon}/X\ll 
\mathfrak{H}(u)\ll P^{d+\varepsilon}/X\}}
\frac{1}{
{\mathfrak{H}(u)^{(n-m)/2}}}
 \mathrm{d} u
 \ll P^\varepsilon \left(\frac{P^d}{X}\right)^{1-(n-m)/2},
\end{align*}
which is satisfactory and so completes the proof of the lemma.
